title: Celebrating the Day of $π$: Joyful Variations on Euler's Identity
summary: This short essay celebrates the mathematical meaning of Pi Day through Euler's formula \[ e^{ix}=\cos x+i\sin x, \] from which Euler's identity \[ e^{iπ}+1=0 \] follows immediately. We briefly note the historical background of the formula, usually traced to Euler's \emph{Introductio in analysin infinitorum} (1748), while also mentioning Roger Cotes's earlier precursor of 1714. We compare Euler's identity, in an explicitly analogical way, with several famous formulas in physics in order to highlight its remarkable compactness and conceptual richness.
